---
title: "UN Voting"
format: pdf
---

```{r}

#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
library(igraph)

votes_data <- read_csv(file.path("~/Desktop", "Voting by UN.csv"))  

# 2. Extract the year safely
votes_data <- votes_data %>%   
  mutate(
    year_text = sub(".*/", "", date),  
    year_num = as.numeric(year_text), 
    year = ifelse(year_num < 100, year_num + 2000, year_num)  
  )

target_countries <- c(
  "UNITED STATES",
  "GERMANY", 
  "CHINA", 
  "RUSSIA", 
  "JAPAN", 
  "UNITED KINGDOM", 
  "CANADA", 
  "SPAIN", 
  "MEXICO", 
  "INDIA", 
  "AUSTRALIA")


y_votes <- votes_data %>%  
  dplyr::filter(ms_vote == "Y") %>%   
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2000 & year <= 2026) %>%
  dplyr::filter(tolower(ms_name) %in% tolower(target_countries) | 
                grepl("United States|United Kingdom|Russian|Korea", ms_name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  select(ms_name, resolution, date) %>%
  # === ADDED CLEANING STEP: Standardize the long names to your exact targets ===
  mutate(ms_name = case_when(
    grepl("Russia", ms_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "RUSSIA",
    grepl("Korea", ms_name, ignore.case = TRUE)  ~ "SOUTH KOREA",
    grepl("United States|USA", ms_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "UNITED STATES",
    grepl("United Kingdom|UK", ms_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "UNITED KINGDOM",
    TRUE ~ toupper(ms_name) # Makes all other countries uppercase to match your style
  ))

setDT(y_votes)

counted_pairs <- y_votes[y_votes, 
                         on = .(resolution, date), 
                         allow.cartesian = TRUE][
                           ms_name != i.ms_name,            
                           .N,                              
                           by = .(ms_name, i.ms_name)]     

setnames(counted_pairs, c("ms_name", "i.ms_name", "N"), c("ms_name_A", "ms_name_B", "n"))

rm(y_votes, votes_data)
gc()


adj_matrix <- counted_pairs %>%   
  pivot_wider(names_from = ms_name_B, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%   
  column_to_rownames(var = "ms_name_A") %>%   
  as.matrix()  

n <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  adj_matrix, 
  mode = "undirected", 
  weighted = TRUE, 
  diag = FALSE
)

summary(n)


bloc_mapping <- data.frame(
  name = c("UNITED STATES", "UNITED KINGDOM", "CANADA", "GERMANY", "SPAIN", "JAPAN", "AUSTRALIA", 
           "CHINA", "RUSSIA", 
           "SOUTH KOREA", "INDIA", "MEXICO"),
  bloc_color = c("skyblue", "skyblue", "skyblue", "skyblue", "skyblue", "skyblue", "skyblue",
                  "tomato", "tomato",
                  "gold", "forestgreen", "forestgreen")
)

# Match the colors onto the network nodes
v_names <- vertex_attr(n, "name")
node_colors <- bloc_mapping$bloc_color[match(v_names, bloc_mapping$name)]
n <- set_vertex_attr(n, "color", value = node_colors)

country_labels <- vertex_attr(n, "name")
raw_weights <- edge_attr(n, "weight")


min_w <- min(raw_weights)
max_w <- max(raw_weights)
scaled_edge_widths <- ((raw_weights - min_w) / (max_w - min_w)) * 8 + 0.5


edge_colors <- ifelse(raw_weights > (max_w - (max_w - min_w)*0.15), 
                      rgb(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7),   # Dark gray for strongest ties
                      rgb(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.2))  # Faint gray for standard ties


par(mar = c(4, 1, 3, 1))

plot(n,
  layout = layout_with_fr,                 # Keeps factions clearly separated
  vertex.size = 24,                        # Easy to read node sizes
  vertex.label = country_labels,      
  vertex.label.cex = 0.7,                 # Bold, sharp text labels
  vertex.label.font = 2,                   
  vertex.label.color = "black",         
  edge.width = scaled_edge_widths,         # Maps true alignment to line thickness
  edge.color = edge_colors,                # Highlights the absolute strongest alliances
  main = "UN Voting Alignment Factions (2000-2026)\nRelative Relationship Strength"
)

# Add the Key (Legend) to the bottom left corner
legend("bottomleft", 
       legend = c("Western / G7 Allies", "Eastern / BRICS Core", "South Korea / East Asia", "Global South / Non-Aligned"), 
       fill = c("skyblue", "tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), 
       bty = "n", 
       cex = 0.8,
       title = "Geopolitical Blocs")

cat("\n======================================================\n")
cat("   TOP 5 STRONGEST VOTING ALLIANCES (HIGHEST OVERLAP)   \n")
cat("======================================================\n")
top_allies <- counted_pairs %>%
  dplyr::filter(ms_name_A < ms_name_B) %>% # Removes duplicate combinations (A-B vs B-A)
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  head(5)

print(top_allies)
```
